suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar and its .integration is accessed without optional chaining. WHY: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws a TypeError, breaking event creation. HOW: Use optional chaining: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When externalCalendarId is undefined, the fallback searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals undefined, which can never match. WHY: updateEvent loses the previous default of event.destinationCalendar.externalId and may call calendar.events.update with an undefined calendarId; deleteEvent falls back to "primary" instead of the intended host calendar. HOW: Fall back to the first destinationCalendar entry, e.g. event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId. The same fix applies to deleteEvent at lines 315-317.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Office365 createEvent still has the old one-argument signature and always uses event.destinationCalendar[0]. WHY: CalendarManager now calls createEvent(calEvent, credential.id), and for collective bookings it expects the credential's matching destination calendar to be selected; Office365 ignores credentialId and writes every host's event to the first destination calendar. HOW: Accept credentialId and select the destinationCalendar entry whose credentialId matches, then use that entry's externalId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Lark createEvent was not updated to accept credentialId and still reads event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. WHY: With multiple destination calendars, Lark events for additional hosts are created in the wrong calendar because the implementation cannot select the calendar matching the credential in use. HOW: Update the signature to (event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) and select event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The slug and requestedSlug metadata conditions were inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. WHY: Non-billing/self-hosted instances no longer store the organization slug, breaking routing, while billing-enabled instances store both slug and requestedSlug, bypassing the verification flow. HOW: Restore the original conditions: write slug when billing is disabled and requestedSlug only when billing is enabled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The recurring-event cancellation branch iterates over all user calendar credentials inside a loop over every calendar reference. WHY: For collective recurring bookings with multiple calendar references, each calendar event is deleted once per reference, producing redundant API calls and 404/not-found errors. HOW: Use only the credential from the current reference (the already-resolved calendarCredential) instead of looping over bookingToDelete.user.credentials.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: After destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, the code does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError. Add optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) or explicitly handle the empty case so the fallback does not crash.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The string "Notes have been hidden by the organizer" is written directly into calEvent.additionalNotes and shown to users in calendar events, but it is not routed through the project's i18n system. The existing TODO even notes this. The PR changed the spelling of this line without resolving the localization gap, so attendees/organizers whose locale is not English still see an untranslated message. Replace the hard-coded string with a translated key (e.g., t("notes_hidden_by_organizer")) and add it to the locale files.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without checking whether `mainHostDestinationCalendar` exists. Since `destinationCalendar` can be `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` per the type, this causes a TypeError for bookings with no destination calendar. Add an explicit guard, e.g. `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")` or check `mainHostDestinationCalendar` first.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Any attendee of a booking is authorized to add arbitrary guests. WHY: An attendee who knows the bookingId can invoke addGuests and inject new recipients into a meeting they do not own, bypassing organizer control and exposing meeting links/calendar events to unintended parties. HOW: Restrict addGuests to the same principals as bookingsProcedure (organizer or collective participant) or gate attendee access behind an explicit organizer/team-admin permission.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The team permission check requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. WHY: `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for ADMIN or OWNER roles; `isTeamOwner` returns true only for OWNER, so pure team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add guests. HOW: Change the operator from `&&` to `||` so either an admin or an owner is authorized.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the raw `guests` input instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` list. WHY: If the request includes an email that is already an attendee, that attendee is filtered out of `uniqueGuests` and no new record is created, but the email logic still treats it as a new guest and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The blacklisted-guest check is case-sensitive. WHY: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased before comparison, but the submitted `guest` email is compared verbatim, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. `BadEmail@example.com`) is accepted. HOW: Normalize the submitted email to lowercase before comparing against the lowercased blacklist.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The onError handler concatenates err.data?.code and t(err.message) and shows it in a toast. If the server ever returns a raw error string instead of a translation key, sensitive details (emails, booking IDs, internal error text) could be exposed to the user. Defensively treat err.message as a key only when it is known to be a key, or fall back to a generic translation such as t("unable_to_add_guests") rather than rendering the server message directly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler filters the input into `uniqueGuests` and persists only those, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered array. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead so the email manager's `newGuests` parameter matches the attendees that were actually added.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable name and the authorization intent are 'admin OR owner', but the expression uses &&, so a team admin who is not also an owner (or vice versa) is incorrectly denied permission to add guests. Change && to ||.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler computes uniqueGuests (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) to create the new attendees, but sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered guests list. That list is used to choose between AttendeeScheduledEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, so a duplicate email in the input will be treated as a new guest and existing attendees will receive the wrong template. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When err.data?.code is undefined the template literal produces the literal string "undefined: ...", and because that string is truthy the friendly fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") is never shown. Only prepend the code when it exists, otherwise use the translated message or fallback.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The uniqueness refine uses `new Set(emails)`, which compares strings case-sensitively. Email addresses are case-insensitive identity data, so `A@example.com` and `a@example.com` pass validation as unique but refer to the same mailbox. Normalize emails with `toLowerCase()` before the Set comparison (and ideally persist the normalized form) to prevent case-variation duplicates and any downstream bypass of case-sensitive attendee or blacklist checks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is defined with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass the check. The identifier says "or" and the surrounding permission logic at line 54 treats it as an either-or gate. Change `&&` to `||` so team admins or team owners can add guests, matching the name and intended behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `Tooltip` for removing an email field hardcodes `content="Remove email"`, bypassing the i18n system used elsewhere in the component. This text reaches the user untranslated. Pass it through the translation function, e.g., `content={t("remove_email")}`, and add the corresponding key to the locale files.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error message is built as `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` ``. The code portion is shown raw (and becomes "undefined:" when `err.data` is missing), so it is not localized and can be confusing. Because `message` is always truthy, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is never used. Build a fully localized message instead of concatenating an untranslated code, or use the translated fallback directly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId instead of the user's id. WHY: The helper's third parameter is documented as userId, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential primary key as calcomUserId and cannot look up the correct user. HOW: Pass credential.userId as the third argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed property names [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which evaluate to a fixed string such as '[object Object]', not a pattern for arbitrary keys. WHY: When credential sync is enabled every token response will fail this schema because it lacks a property literally named by that string, causing parseRefreshTokenResponse to throw 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. HOW: Replace the computed keys with a passthrough object schema or z.record.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The result of parseRefreshTokenResponse (a SafeParseReturnType wrapper { success, data }) is stored directly as the credential key. WHY: The next load calls googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), which expects the parsed credential shape at the top level, not an object nested under a data property; this breaks the credential after any refresh. HOW: Extract tokenResponse.data before storing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After refreshOAuthTokens, the code reads res?.data, but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response object which has no .data property. WHY: token becomes undefined, so token.access_token throws a runtime error and the calendar refresh crashes. HOW: Normalize the helper output or fall back to parsing the Response JSON.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The code refreshes the access token, writes the new token to the database, then constructs the jsforce Connection using the old credentialKey.access_token. WHY: The refresh is effectively wasted and the connection may be initialized with an expired access token. HOW: Use the refreshed token data when building the connection.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The webhook secret is compared with the !== operator. WHY: String comparison short-circuits on the first mismatching byte, allowing an attacker to brute-force the secret one byte at a time via timing analysis. HOW: Compare secrets with crypto.timingSafeEqual after length check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The handler reads the credential with findFirst and then decides to update or create, but the Credential model has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). WHY: Two concurrent webhook requests for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both insert, producing duplicate credential rows. HOW: Add a @@unique([userId, appId]) constraint and use prisma.credential.upsert with a composite key, or wrap the create in a retry on unique-violation.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout or abort signal. WHY: If the external endpoint hangs, the calling calendar/video request also hangs indefinitely, consuming workers and potentially blocking user-facing operations. HOW: Add an AbortController with a timeout and handle abort errors.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is validated with a direct `!==` string comparison (`req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). This is vulnerable to timing attacks because string comparison short-circuits at the first differing byte, allowing an attacker to iteratively guess the secret. Use a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after normalizing both values to equal-length buffers, or wrap the comparison in a dedicated constant-time helper.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` uses an empty string fallback if the encryption key environment variable is not set. This silently degrades security and could allow decryption/derivation with a known weak key. Fail fast instead (throw or return an error) when the encryption key is missing or shorter than the required 32 bytes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) is not wrapped in try/catch. If the request body is malformed or fails validation, the thrown ZodError becomes an unhandled exception instead of a controlled 400 response. Use safeParse and return a 400 JSON error, or wrap parse in try/catch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The decrypted `keys` string is passed directly to JSON.parse and then stored in Prisma without validating the object shape. If decryption produces non-JSON plaintext or an attacker supplies a malformed payload, this throws unhandled or writes arbitrary data into the credential key column. Validate the parsed shape before persisting and handle parse/decryption errors.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: decodeOAuthState does a bare JSON.parse(req.query.state). A malformed or tampered `state` query param throws SyntaxError, crashing the OAuth callback handler. Use a try/catch and return undefined or a controlled error. The same issue exists in encodeOAuthState.ts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as keys. `toString()` on a ZodString object does not return a wildcard pattern; it returns the object's string representation, so these keys do not validate arbitrary numeric/optional fields as intended. As a result expiry fields are not enforced and invalid token responses may pass validation, corrupting stored credentials. Use `z.record(z.string(), z.number())` or a proper index signature instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The guard uses `userId` in a boolean context, so a user id of `0` is treated as absent and the code falls back to the local refresh instead of calling the configured `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Because the parameter is typed `number | null`, the only value that should disable sync is `null` (team credentials). Use an explicit `userId !== null` check so `0` is handled like any other valid user id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The schema tries to accept any numeric property as an expiry field, but `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so the validator does not actually allow arbitrary provider response fields and may reject valid responses. Rewrite the schema to genuinely permit extra keys, for example by using `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` and checking separately that at least one extra value is a number.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `SafeParseReturnType` object (with `success` and `data` properties), but this caller assigns that wrapper directly to `key` and writes it to Prisma. Other callers in the same PR read `tokenResponse.data`. The caller should extract `.data` before persisting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` names its third parameter `userId` and forwards it as `calcomUserId` to the credential-sync endpoint. The Zoho Bigin call site passes `credentialId`, so when credential sync is enabled the parent application receives the wrong identifier and cannot look up the correct user. Pass the Cal.com user id (e.g. `credential.userId`) instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is configured, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response. Callers consume the result in incompatible ways: Google Calendar reads `res.data`, Hubspot casts to `HubspotToken`, and Zoho Bigin checks `.data.error`, while other callers pass the result to fetch helpers. This cross-site disagreement will fail at runtime for the integrations that expect provider-specific response objects. Normalize the helper's return value to the same shape the original refresh function would produce, or make callers branch on whether the sync path was used.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is named `userId` and is forwarded to the credential-sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId` instead, so the endpoint receives a credential ID mislabeled as a user ID. Pass the credential's owner (`credential.userId` or equivalent) like the other calendar/video adapters do.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod safe-parse result object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credentials. The code stores the whole result object in Prisma, so the credential key will contain the `success` wrapper. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or handle the success check) before updating the credential.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is on, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response, but this caller expects the google-auth shape `{ res: { data: ... } }` and reads `res?.data`. In sync mode `res.data` is undefined, causing `token.access_token` to throw. Either normalize the sync response in `refreshOAuthTokens` or handle the Response shape here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the try block, not only for SMS scheduling failures. WHY: Failures from `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, or other unrelated setup can mark a reminder for deletion even though Twilio was never attempted. HOW: Wrap only the `twilio.scheduleSMS` call and the successful update in try/catch, or restructure so retryCount is incremented only when scheduling itself fails.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The deleteMany second OR branch deletes WorkflowReminder rows with retryCount > 1 without filtering by method. WHY: This cron job is scoped to SMS reminders, but the new condition would also delete email or other-method reminders if any future code increments their retryCount. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch so both disjuncts are method-scoped.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cron job's deleteMany queries `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` on WorkflowReminder, but there is no index on the new retryCount column. WHY: The OR branch has no method filter, so the planner cannot use the existing `method, scheduled, scheduledDate` index for it; on a large table this can become a sequential scan every cron run. HOW: Add an index on `retryCount` (e.g., `@@index([retryCount])` or `@@index([method, retryCount])`) in schema.prisma and the migration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says it deletes only past-due scheduled SMS reminders, but the query now also deletes reminders of any method or date whose retryCount is greater than 1. Update the comment so future maintainers do not assume the cleanup is limited to SMS/past-due rows.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The catch block logs the raw `error` object from SMS scheduling. Provider error responses often include PII such as recipient/sender phone numbers and message bodies. Redact or summarize the error before logging (e.g., log only the provider error code and a generic message) to prevent leaking sensitive data into application logs.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The second branch of the deleteMany OR condition (retryCount > 1) does not include method: WorkflowMethods.SMS. WorkflowReminder is shared between SMS and EMAIL methods, so this branch can silently delete email reminders if retryCount is ever set on them. Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch to keep the cleanup scoped to SMS reminders, matching the comment and the findMany query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch in the `deleteMany` filter is not restricted to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron can now delete email/other-method workflow reminders that use the same `retryCount` column. This changes the behavior contract of the endpoint for any non-SMS consumer of `WorkflowReminder` without updating those consumers. Scope the whole cleanup to SMS reminders.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup code verification compares the user-supplied code without normalizing case. WHY: Generated backup codes are lowercase hex, so a user who types an otherwise valid code in uppercase is rejected as incorrect. HOW: Lower-case the stripped input before comparing, e.g. `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "").toLowerCase()`, and apply the same normalization in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code authentication branch does not itself verify the user's password. WHY: Password verification is gated by `!credentials.totpCode`, so an attacker who knows a backup code can bypass the password by also sending any non-empty totpCode and authenticate successfully. HOW: Verify the password inside the backup-code branch (or move password verification before the second-factor branches) before consuming the backup code.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The clipboard writeText call is not awaited and its errors are not handled. WHY: The success toast is shown immediately even if the browser rejects the copy (permission denied, insecure context, etc.), misleading the user and leaving an unhandled promise rejection. HOW: Await the clipboard call and only show the toast on success, or catch errors and show an error toast.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The component is exported as `TwoFactor` but the file is `BackupCode.tsx` and is imported as `BackupCode`. Rename the function to `BackupCode` so the identifier matches the file name and usage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The assertion `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes even when the switch is not checked because `locator.isChecked()` returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy when passed to the generic `toBeTruthy()` matcher. The PR added a FIXME noting this exact failure mode but left the assertion in place. Replace it with `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`)).toBeChecked()` or `await expect(await page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBe(true)` so the test actually fails when the switch is unchecked.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: After clicking the copy button, the test only waits for `toast-success`, but the implementation in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting it and unconditionally shows the success toast. If the clipboard write fails or writes the wrong text, the toast still appears and the test passes. Read the clipboard (e.g., `await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())`) and assert it contains the expected backup codes.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup-code comparison uses `backupCodes.indexOf(...replaceAll("-", ""))`, which short-circuits on mismatch and leaks timing information about the stored secret codes. Replace it with a constant-time comparison over every code (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) and decide the match only after the loop, so an attacker cannot learn which code is correct or how much of it they guessed.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The disable endpoint locates the supplied backup code with `backupCodes.indexOf(...replaceAll("-", ""))`. This performs a non-constant-time secret comparison and can leak information through response timing. Compare every stored code with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and only return success/failure after evaluating all candidates.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The default-exported function in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` while the file and all imports use the name `BackupCode`. This naming inconsistency makes component identity in DevTools, error stacks and code search misleading and looks like a copy-paste error from TwoFactor.tsx. Rename the function to `BackupCode` to match its actual usage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Tests assert equality between flat Prisma.sql template literals and nested Prisma.sql compositions returned by the service. WHY: The service builds compound conditions by interpolating Prisma.Sql fragments into other Prisma.sql templates (e.g., buildFilterConditions and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition), producing Sql objects whose values array contains nested Sql objects; Jest toEqual compares enumerable strings/values properties, so the flat expected literals will not match the nested actual values and the tests will fail. HOW: Assert on the emitted SQL text instead, e.g., expect(conditions.text).toEqual(expected.text), or use a helper that normalizes Prisma.Sql to its flattened text/values before comparison.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `this.filters.eventTypeId` and `this.filters.memberUserId` are optional `number`s, but the code tests them with `if (this.filters.eventTypeId)` and `if (this.filters.memberUserId)`. A caller passing the perfectly valid numeric ID `0` will be treated as if no filter was supplied, causing rows for ID 0 to be excluded or, worse, included when they shouldn't be. Use explicit null/undefined checks such as `this.filters.eventTypeId != null` or `typeof this.filters.eventTypeId !== "undefined"` instead of truthiness.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`. When the organization has no child teams, `teamIds` is empty and PostgreSQL cannot infer the element type of the empty array parameter, causing a runtime error. Guard the team branch the same way the user branch is guarded, and fall back to `1=0` (NOTHING_CONDITION) when both lists are empty.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for scope "team", but buildTeamAuthorizationCondition assumes it is defined and interpolates `options.teamId` directly into Prisma.sql. Either keep the schema discriminated-union type in the constructor (requiring teamId for team scope) or validate/throw before using options.teamId, so the previous invariant is not broken.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The exported `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type marks `teamId` as optional, but the `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` and the team-scope authorization logic require it. A caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId`; runtime validation fails, `this.options` is set to `null`, and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `Prisma.sql`1=0``, producing empty results with no error. Align the public type with the schema so missing `teamId` is caught at compile time, e.g. replace the manual type with `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>` or use a discriminated union that requires `teamId` for `scope: "team"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Protocol-relative URLs such as '//cdn.example.com/foo' are rewritten to 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/foo'. WHY: The code strips all leading slashes from any href/src starting with '/' and then prefixes the base host, so protocol-relative links break and point at the wrong host. HOW: Skip or separately handle protocol-relative URLs; only rewrite single-slash relative paths.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The scheduled job calls i.content.scrub without checking whether i.content exists. WHY: Many RSS/Atom feeds provide only a description or summary, so i.content is nil and the job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed import. HOW: Guard against nil content, falling back to an empty string or the item's description/summary.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The script immediately calls comments.appendChild(iframe) without verifying that document.getElementById('discourse-comments') returned an element. WHY: If the host page omits the container or loads the script before the element exists, comments is null and appendChild throws, breaking other scripts on the page. HOW: Guard the appendChild call with an if (comments) check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import appends the 'Imported from' footer to the input contents string using <<, mutating the caller's object. WHY: In-place mutation can corrupt reused strings and raises RuntimeError when the caller passes a frozen string; it also makes the function's side effects unpredictable. HOW: Build a new string instead of mutating the parameter.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without verifying the setting is present. WHY: If feed polling is disabled and embed_by_username is blank, the retrieve job raises NoMethodError on nil.downcase instead of failing gracefully. HOW: Return early when the username setting is blank, matching the guard in PollFeed.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the current job. WHY: This blocks the Sidekiq worker while the entire feed is fetched and every item is imported, even though only the requested embed_url is needed. HOW: Either look up only the specific embed_url in the feed, or enqueue PollFeed asynchronously and let the loading page continue polling.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: poll_feed calls open(feed_url).read without a timeout and iterates rss.items without any limit. WHY: A slow or unresponsive feed can hold a worker indefinitely, and a very large feed can consume excessive memory and time importing every item. HOW: Add a read timeout to open and cap the number of items processed per run.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Compare `URI(request.referer || '').host` with `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` case-insensitively, e.g. by downcasing both sides. DNS host names are case-insensitive, so a referer with uppercase letters (or an uppercase configured host) will incorrectly fail the embedding allow-list check.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Downcase both `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and `URI(@embed_url).host` before comparing them. Host names are case-insensitive, so mixed-case or uppercase URLs may bypass or incorrectly fail the host allow-list check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tests 'does not call perform_retrieve when embeddable_host is not set', 'different than the host of the URL', and 'embed url is not a url' stub SiteSetting.embeddable_host and assert that perform_retrieve is never called. But they also stub retrieve_recently? implicitly only in later tests. The implementation's invalid_host? raises URI::InvalidURIError; if invalid_host? were removed or always returned false, retrieve_recently? would still gate perform_retrieve. Because perform_retrieve is the actual private method being mocked, a bug in invalid_host? does not cause these tests to fail; the tests exercise the mock, not the real host-matching logic. Replace the mock of perform_retrieve with direct assertion about the side effect (e.g. no HTTP fetch, no TopicEmbed import) or call invalid_host? directly and assert its result.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' and 'creates a topic view' tests stub TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed, TopicRetriever.new, TopicView.new, and the retriever's retrieve method. They therefore pass even if the controller action's real logic for calling TopicRetriever, TopicView, or rendering 'loading' is removed or inverted. These tests assert only that mocks are called with the expected arguments, which by construction matches the test setup; they do not verify the actual response body, template, or that an embed record is created. Add expectations on response.body/rendered_template (e.g. assert the loading partial is rendered when no topic exists and the topic view partial is rendered when one exists) and use real collaborators or at least assert the side effects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The execute tests stub all three SiteSetting predicates and assert that poll_feed is or is not called. If the execute method's guard condition were changed to ignore any of those settings (e.g. always call poll_feed), the tests using stubs with expects(:poll_feed).never would still catch it, but the 'delegates to poll_feed' test only verifies that poll_feed is called once when all settings are stubbed true; it does not verify that poll_feed actually opens the configured URL, parses it, or calls TopicEmbed.import. The poll_feed method itself has no dedicated test. Add a test that stubs an RSS response and asserts TopicEmbed.import is called with the expected arguments, otherwise a broken parser or wrong argument order could go undetected.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration adds cook_method with default: 1, but Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), which maps :regular => 0 and :raw_html => 1. Therefore every existing post and any new post created without an explicit cook_method will be treated as raw_html; Post#cook will return raw instead of cooked HTML, breaking topic rendering across the site. The default should be 0 so the regular cooking pipeline remains the default.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The line `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` directly on `i.content`. If a feed item has no content element (for example a summary-only Atom entry or an empty RSS item), `i.content` is nil and the job raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll. Guard against nil content before scrubbing/unescaping, e.g. `content = CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || '').scrub)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`, but `Post.cook_methods` defines `:regular` as 0 and `:raw_html` as 1. This causes all existing posts to default to `raw_html` and skip cooking, returning raw markdown instead of rendered HTML. Change the default to `0` so existing posts keep the regular cooked behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Post.cook_methods maps :regular to 0 and :raw_html to 1, but the migration defaults cook_method to 1. Existing posts will therefore be treated as raw_html and skip the cooking pipeline, rendering raw content instead of cooked HTML.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. ERB emits `end if` verbatim into the generated Ruby source, which is invalid syntax after a multi-line if/else block and will cause the template to raise a syntax error when rendered.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The feed_key helper builds a cache key, but neither execute nor poll_feed calls it, so the computation is dead code. Remove it or wire it into feed polling (for example, to skip unchanged feeds via Redis).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` fetch a host with `.first` and use it without checking for nil. WHY: A request with a non-existent ID causes `NoMethodError` when `save_host` assigns `host.host = ...` or when `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, returning a 500 instead of a clean 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound → 404) or guard nil and `render_json_error` / head 404.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The migration interpolates values from `site_settings` directly into an INSERT statement. WHY: An admin who previously set `embeddable_hosts` to a value containing a single quote can inject arbitrary SQL that runs with full database privileges during migration. HOW: Use parameterized SQL or escape each host value before interpolation.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `record_for_host` queries with `lower(host) = ?` but the table has no index on `host`. WHY: This lookup runs on every embedded request, and as the allowed-hosts list grows it degrades to a full table scan. HOW: Add an index on `host` in the migration, ideally `lower(host)` if the database supports expression indexes, or a standard btree index with case-insensitive comparisons in the query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fabricator file contents are swapped between `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. WHY: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, while category-related fabricators were moved to `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, making the file names misleading and breaking the convention that a fabricator file defines the model named in its filename. HOW: Move the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators back to `category_fabricator.rb`, and keep `:embeddable_host` in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import` now passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)`, which becomes nil when no embeddable host matches the URL. WHY: Previously the default `SiteSetting.embed_category` was always used; feed polling and import scripts that call `import` directly can now create topics with no explicit category, changing behavior for URLs that do not match a configured host. HOW: Fall back to the uncategorized category or the old default when `eh` is blank, matching the controller's blank-category handling.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: In record_for_host, the query uses `lower(host) = ?` but passes `uri.host` without downcasing it. If the stored value or database collation is case-sensitive, comparison semantics become inconsistent and a case-variation host can bypass or fail the allowlist unexpectedly. Normalize both sides consistently: downcase `uri.host` before comparing, and consider downcasing `self.host` in before_validation so stored hosts are always lowercase.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration splits the old site setting value on `\n` and inserts each segment directly into SQL. Old values may contain empty lines, whitespace, protocol prefixes, or trailing paths, but the migration bypasses the model's `before_validation` normalization and the format validation. Use `h.strip` to discard blanks and rely on `EmbeddableHost.create!` (or explicitly apply the same strip logic as the model) instead of raw SQL so the validation/normalization callbacks run.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `record_for_host` builds a URI, extracts `uri.host`, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. The right-hand side is not downcased, so a stored host such as `EvilTrout.com` will be compared as `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` and fail to match. Downcase the extracted host before the query to make matching case-insensitive as intended.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` treats `0` and empty string the same as `nil`. If category id `0` is ever meaningful, it will be silently replaced. Use `if host.category_id.nil?` to test for an explicitly absent value rather than any falsy/blank value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `update` does `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately passes the result to `save_host`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the id does not exist, these actions raise `NoMethodError`. Return a 404/not-found response when the record is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The describe block is named 'allows_embeddable_host' but the model method added in this PR is 'host_allowed?'. The test description names a non-existent method, which is confusing and will break navigation/expectations. Rename the describe block to 'host_allowed?' to match the actual API.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The input placeholder is hardcoded English text 'example.com' instead of using the I18n translation mechanism. This bypasses localization and will appear untranslated for non-English users. Add a translation key (e.g. admin.embedding.host_placeholder) and use it here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The spec added for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only checks that it is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. It does not exercise create, update, or destroy. Those actions could be completely broken and this spec would still pass, so it does not verify the controller behaviour it appears to cover. Add request specs for the actual actions, or at least assert that saving/destroying a host has the expected side effects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The spec added for Admin::EmbeddingController only checks that it inherits from Admin::AdminController. It does not call show or update, which in this PR return a serialized embedding object. Those actions could be removed or broken and the spec would still pass. Add tests that hit the routes and verify the serialized response contains the embeddable hosts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' builds a default topic and asserts expandable_first_post? is false. The implementation no longer depends on embeddable hosts, and the body does not configure or assert anything about them; the assertion passes because embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? are false by default. Rename the test to match what it actually checks (e.g. 'is false by default') or make it explicitly exercise the embeddable_host condition and assert the method returns false for that reason.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. When the id is not found, `update` passes `nil` into `save_host`, which then calls `host.host = ...` and raises `NoMethodError`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on `nil`. This produces a 500 error for a missing resource instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and is handled by the base controller) or explicitly guard for `host.blank?` and render a 404.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration fetches `embed_category` and `uncategorized_category_id` with `execute(...)[0]['id']` / `[0]['value']`. If either setting is missing, `[0]` is nil and the migration fails. Use safe row access (`rows.first`) and provide a sensible default so the migration can run on databases that lack those settings.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category` fabricators. Swap the contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name indicates.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a valid CSS property. WHY: IE10/11 ignore this declaration; while the correct `-ms-flex-align` is also present, the invalid line is dead code that contradicts the mixin's intent of covering all prefixes and may mislead future maintainers. HOW: Remove the invalid `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` line.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real CSS property and will be ignored by browsers. The correct Microsoft-prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already included on the previous line. Remove the invalid `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` declaration to avoid dead/wrong CSS output.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so `.topic-avatar` is a flex item and its `float: left` declaration is ignored by the flex layout algorithm. Remove the dead `float: left` from `.topic-avatar` since the horizontal placement is now handled by flexbox.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: A second `downsize` class method with a different arity overrides the first, because Ruby redefines singleton methods rather than overloading by arity. WHY: The existing caller `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` passes `(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which the surviving signature maps as `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`, causing `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for 100:Integer` when `downsize_instructions` reads `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. HOW: Remove the duplicate and keep a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` method; update `resize_emoji.rb` to call `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, '100x100', opts)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but discards its return value. WHY: `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` when ImageMagick fails or raises an exception, so a failed resize leaves the original oversized tempfile intact and `Upload.create_for` still stores it, allowing uploads that exceed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. HOW: Check the return value and abort or skip the upload when downsizing fails, e.g. `break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` inside the loop and validate the final size before creating the upload.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149, which overrides the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Ruby method definitions with the same name shadow earlier ones, so the 4-argument version is never callable. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will invoke the 3-argument version, binding the width to `dimensions` and the height to `opts`, producing wrong arguments for `optimize`. Rename the new method (e.g., `downsize_by_dimensions`) or keep a single `downsize` implementation that handles both calling conventions correctly.

suggestions.label: duplicate-definition
suggestions.suggestionContent: Duplicate `downsize` method definition: the definition at lines 145-147 is immediately overridden by the definition at lines 149-151. This is an implementation issue (not a test defect) and falls outside the assigned defect class, but it is the only concrete issue described in the diff.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR redefines OptimizedImage.downsize to accept a dimensions string (e.g., '80%') instead of separate width/height arguments, but leaves the old four-argument wrapper at lines 145-147. Ruby method definitions override rather than overload, so the new three-argument definition at lines 149-151 silently replaces the old one. Any caller still using the previous four-argument contract (from, to, max_width, max_height) will have max_width treated as the dimensions string and max_height treated as opts, producing incorrect image geometry or an error. Remove the shadowed four-argument downsize definition so only the intended contract remains.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The file now defines OptimizedImage.downsize twice: first with signature (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and then with (from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Ruby silently uses the last definition, so the 4-argument version is dead code and any existing caller that passes separate width/height values will raise ArgumentError. Remove the first (4-argument) definition, or if backwards compatibility is required keep only one method and make the second form a wrapper.

suggestions.label: method-redefinition
suggestions.suggestionContent: The duplicate downsize() method definition is a Ruby method-redefinition concern (a later definition silently overrides the earlier one). This is outside the assigned defect class but worth verifying that the redefinition is intentional and that the earlier definition is removed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR adds a second `downsize` class method with a different signature right after the first one. Ruby has no method overloading by arity, so the second definition replaces the first, making the `max_width`/`max_height` signature unreachable. Any caller that still passes separate width/height arguments will now hit the wrong method body and likely raise an ArgumentError. Remove the now-dead first definition (or merge both signatures into a single method that detects whether it received a dimensions string or width/height pair).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The model declares `downsize` with both a 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` signature and a 3-argument `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` signature. Ruby silently shadows the first with the second, so the controller's new call at uploads_controller.rb:67 (passing a percentage string) only matches the second definition and any existing caller using the old width/height form will raise ArgumentError. Remove the stale 4-argument definition so the contract matches the controller's usage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` asks ImageMagick to read from and write to the same file. The model's `convert_with` builds a `convert <from> ... <to>` shell command and assumes distinct paths; overwriting the source during conversion can corrupt or truncate the upload. Downsize to a temporary path and then replace the original.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. WHY: With 100 members and a page size of 50 it reports 3 total pages instead of 2, so `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and `next()` navigates to an empty page. HOW: Replace the formula with `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `members` action now reads `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` without enforcing a maximum. WHY: The previous implementation capped automatic groups at 200 members per request; that cap is gone, so any user who can view a group can request an unbounded number of records (e.g. `?limit=9999999`), causing a large DB query and memory load. HOW: Cap the limit to a reasonable maximum such as `limit = [[params[:limit].to_i, 200].min, 1].max` or equivalent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The add_members and remove_member actions read params.require(:group_id), but the routes declared in config/routes.rb are member routes under `resources :groups`, so Rails supplies the group id as `params[:id]`. This mismatch will cause ParameterMissing on every add/remove request. Change `params.require(:group_id)` to `params.require(:id)` (or declare the routes with `param: :group_id`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50 or 100/50) it reports one page too many. That makes showingLast false on the last populated page and lets the Next action advance to offset == user_count, where findMembers returns no rows. Replace it with Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (and guard limit == 0).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead of Math.floor(...)+1. With the current formula, a group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports 2 total pages, so the pager enables "next" and shows an empty page 2.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: params[:alias_level].present? returns false for the integer 0, so selecting the "nobody" alias level (value 0) leaves the existing alias_level unchanged. Use an existence check that accepts 0 while still skipping absent/blank values.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The totalPages formula uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one larger than the actual page count whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. This makes showingLast false on the real last page and allows navigation to an empty final page. Replace the calculation with Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) inside the existing zero guard.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The route config/routes.rb maps remove_member to `delete "members"`, but this test sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. The HTTP method does not match the declared endpoint, so the test does not exercise the real route and documents the wrong API contract. Change `:put` to `:delete`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves the underlying hash empty, so every method other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `keys`, `defaults`, `map`) sees an empty collection. WHY: This violates the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks/Hash contract; any future caller that iterates or inspects `I18n.fallbacks` will get no locales even though `I18n.fallbacks[:en]` returns a fallback chain. HOW: Delegate storage to a real Hash by calling `super` in `[]` and populating defaults explicitly, or do not inherit from Hash and instead implement only the small interface I18n::Backend::Fallbacks actually needs (e.g. `def [](locale); ... end`).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache before the database write succeeds, so a failed CreateOrUpdateDevice leaves a cached entry that suppresses limit checks for 29 minutes. WHY: after the first ErrDeviceLimitReached rejection, retries from the same device hit the cache and skip the store, allowing anonymous authentication to bypass the configured device limit. HOW: move a.localCache.SetDefault to after a successful a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device) return, or invalidate the cache on error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice checks CountDevices and then performs the insert/update in separate, non-atomic steps. WHY: concurrent requests can both see count < deviceLimit and both insert new devices, allowing the number of stored devices to exceed the configured anonymous device limit. HOW: wrap the count check and write in a single transaction with an appropriate isolation level, or enforce the limit with a single set-returning query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices and then conditionally inserts in two separate transactions. Two concurrent requests can both read count < deviceLimit and both insert new rows, overshooting the configured anonymous device limit. Enforce the limit atomically (e.g., with a single UPSERT guarded by a subquery count, a serializable transaction, or an application-level lock) so the check and write happen together.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateDevice updates only rows WHERE updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt - 30d AND device.UpdatedAt + 1m. If the existing row's updated_at is older than 30 days, the UPDATE matches no rows and CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The caller in client.go then fails anonymous authentication. The limit-reached path should still allow an existing device to be renewed/updated regardless of age (or fall back to an insert when the device_id already exists), rather than rejecting the request.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error message 'device limit reached' is user-facing but is a hard-coded English literal. It bypasses Grafana's i18n/translation system, so users in other locales will see untranslated English text. This string should be passed through the project's translation mechanism (e.g., i18n.Translate) and added to the relevant locale file(s).

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The write lock is held while performing blocking file I/O or an HTTP request to the CDN. WHY: Every concurrent request that needs web assets is serialized behind that single I/O operation, causing a startup/request-time bottleneck. HOW: Perform the asset loading outside the lock and only acquire the lock to read or update the cache pointer; alternatively use sync.Once for initial population and an atomic pointer for reads.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After acquiring the write lock, the function does not re-check whether another goroutine already populated the cache, and it assigns `result` to the cache even when `result` is nil due to an error. WHY: A later goroutine that failed to load assets can overwrite a previously successful cache entry with nil, causing every subsequent non-Dev request to re-read the manifest and defeating the cache. HOW: Add a double-checked read after acquiring the write lock and only update the cache when the load succeeded.

The double-check pattern is missing after taking the write lock. This is an internal concurrency/performance issue (not a contract change visible to callers): after acquiring the write lock, the cache should be re-checked before reading the manifest and populating it, to avoid redundant work under concurrent access.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: After acquiring entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(), GetWebAssets should re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache is already non-nil (and cfg.Env != setting.Dev) before reading the manifest again. Without that second check, multiple goroutines that both passed the initial read-locked nil check will perform the file/CDN read sequentially and overwrite the cache, causing duplicate work and possible inconsistent cached values. Add a guarded re-check immediately after the Lock().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware returns a middleware closure that reuses the same *MetricsMiddleware instance and mutates its `next` field. WHY: Decorating more than one client with the returned middleware overwrites the chain and, because the metrics are already registered on the same registerer, a second factory use can panic with duplicate metric registration. HOW: Inside the closure create a new *MetricsMiddleware (or a shallow copy of the registered metrics struct) with its own `next` pointer, registering the metrics only once at factory construction time.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin target from the registry twice per request (once for size and once for duration). WHY: The duplicated registry lookup doubles the work on every plugin request for the two instrumented endpoints. HOW: Resolve the target once per method and pass it into both instrumentPluginRequestSize and instrumentPluginRequest, or add a helper that records size and duration with a single lookup.

suggestions.label: documentation/name mismatch
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test function name `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` still uses the old 'Instrumentation' name while the middleware is now called `MetricsMiddleware`. This is a minor naming inconsistency but not user-facing and only affects test naming.

suggestions.label: documentation inaccuracy
suggestions.suggestionContent: The doc comment for `pluginRequestSize` says 'returned' which appears inaccurate (it tracks outgoing request sizes), but this is in internal metric help text.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test function is named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`, but the PR renamed the middleware to `MetricsMiddleware` (the file is `metrics_middleware_test.go` and the type is `MetricsMiddleware`). Rename the test to `TestMetricsMiddleware` so it matches the implementation and is discovered by name-filtered test runs such as `go test -run TestMetricsMiddleware`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Create fails, the code records a legacy-duration metric instead of a storage-duration metric. WHY: This corrupts the dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds histogram with values from the unified store and makes the storage-error path invisible in the storage metric. HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` in the error branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Update fails, the code records a legacy-duration metric instead of a storage-duration metric. WHY: It misattributes the unified-store error to the legacy store and leaves the storage-duration histogram without an error observation. HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` in the error branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records a storage-duration metric for the legacy call. WHY: It puts legacy-call latency into the dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds histogram and leaves the legacy histogram without an observation. HOW: Use `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` inside the goroutine.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: On successful Delete, the storage-duration metric is observed with `name` as the third label instead of `options.Kind`. WHY: The third histogram label is `kind`; passing the object name creates inconsistent label values across methods and inflates metric cardinality with unique names. HOW: Pass `options.Kind` to match the error path and other methods.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The goroutines spawned for async legacy writes are created from the request context using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. WHY: The request context is canceled when the HTTP handler returns, so the async legacy write is likely canceled before it completes, defeating mode 3's purpose of writing to legacy as a safety measure. HOW: Detach the goroutine context from request cancellation, e.g. `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), time.Second*10, ...)` so it can run to completion or its own timeout.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection spawns a new goroutine that can live up to 10 seconds with no concurrency limit or backpressure. WHY: Under high write throughput this creates unbounded goroutine fanout and memory growth, especially if the legacy store is slow or times out. HOW: Bound concurrency with a worker pool or semaphore, or use a rate-limited background queue for legacy writes.

suggestions.label: fragile test mock
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test file constructs a single shared *mock.Mock and embeds it in both legacyStoreMock and storageMock, which define separate mock methods over the same underlying mock object. Because both d.Storage.Create and d.Legacy.Create route through that single shared Mock, expectations are matched against whichever method name the concrete type invokes. This works only because the mock instance is shared, so the test is fragile and relies on that shared-instance coupling rather than on distinct, independent mocks.

suggestions.label: metric label inconsistency
suggestions.suggestionContent: Inconsistent metric recording in the production DualWriterMode3 code: recordStorageDuration is used versus recordLegacyDuration, and options.Kind/name are used inconsistently (for example, the Delete success path records name instead of options.Kind). This is a single-hunk issue rather than a cross-file disagreement, but the labels/names recorded are inconsistent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In Delete, `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` is computed but never used. The next line does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, so the enriched `log` is discarded and context logs lose the name/kind/method tags. It should use `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` like the other methods.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `d.Storage.Create` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. It should call `recordStorageDuration` because the failure came from Storage, not Legacy. As written, the storage error path is credited to the legacy metric with the storage start time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. It should call `recordStorageDuration`, matching the Delete path. The storage failure is currently attributed to Legacy.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: After a successful Storage Delete, the code records `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. All other metric calls in this file use `options.Kind` as the resource/kind label. This mismatch will break queries/dashboards that group by kind. It should use `options.Kind` to stay consistent with the error path and other methods.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success case 'deleting an object in the unified store' only configures a mock for Storage.Delete and asserts only the synchronous result. The implementation also spawns a goroutine that calls Legacy.Delete, but the test exits immediately. If the legacy write were removed from the implementation, this test would still pass. Worse, because no expectation is registered for Legacy.Delete, the test can panic if the goroutine runs before the test returns, making it flaky.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success case 'deleting a collection in the unified store' only mocks Storage.DeleteCollection. The implementation spawns a goroutine that also calls Legacy.DeleteCollection, but the test does not register that expectation and returns before the goroutine completes. This means the test passes even if the legacy collection deletion is removed, and it may panic on a slow run when the unmocked legacy call executes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success case is named 'creating an object only in the unified store', but the implementation also writes to LegacyStorage in a goroutine. The test registers a Legacy.Create mock but never asserts it is called, so the test would still pass if the legacy write were entirely removed. The test name should match the actual dual-write behaviour and the test should verify the legacy call is attempted, or use a synchronization primitive to wait for the goroutine.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Update passes the same `objInfo` to `d.Storage.Update` synchronously and then to `d.Legacy.Update` in a goroutine. Because `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` may hold mutable state and `UpdatedObject` can produce different results when invoked at different times or against different stored objects, Storage and Legacy may apply different versions of the update, violating the dual-write consistency invariant and creating a data race. The previous code pre-computed the updated object and wrapped it for both stores; that synchronization should be preserved or a copy/thread-safe wrapper should be used.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: At line 45, when `d.Storage.Create` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This records the storage failure under the legacy duration/error metric, corrupting the metric labels. It should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: At line 129, when `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. The failure is in Storage, not Legacy, so it should be recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: At line 166, the goroutine performing `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)`. Because the operation is on LegacyStorage, it should call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test case 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' still sets up a Legacy.Create mock expectation, but the new DualWriterMode3.Create contract (lines 42-46) returns immediately when Storage.Create fails and never calls Legacy.Create. Update this test to match the new contract: remove the Legacy expectation in the storage-failure path and assert that Legacy.Create is not invoked. If the intent is to verify the new async path, add synchronization so the goroutine is observed before assertions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Removing the coarse cacheMu lock at the start of BuildIndex leaves concurrent calls for the same NamespacedResource key unsynchronized. WHY: Two goroutines that reach BuildIndex for the same key (e.g., concurrent Search requests or a Search racing with a watch event via getOrCreateIndex) both create indexes; for file-backed indexes they collide on the same directory, and the second writer overwrites the first in the cache without closing it, leaking the index. HOW: Reintroduce per-key synchronization that still allows different keys to build concurrently—check the cache under a per-key lock/mutex before starting, return the existing index if present, and only write the newly built index if no other builder won the race.

suggestions.label: Behavioral contract change: Init now called during construction
suggestions.suggestionContent: NewResourceServer now invokes s.Init(ctx) during construction (lines 258-262), which is a behavioral contract change: construction previously returned a server that still required a separate Init call. Any consumer that calls Init after construction would be affected, though no such consumer-side breakage is visible in the changed code in this diff.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, but `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` and leaves `rule` undefined. WHY: Clicking the Silence action in the Grafana rule list menu sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the drawer never mounts, so users cannot silence Grafana rules from the list view. HOW: Also check the prom rule type, e.g. change the condition to `(rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)) && showSilenceDrawer`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `GrafanaRuleListItem` rendered for `origin === 'grafana'` omits the `key` prop, while the `datasource` and `default` branches include `key={key}`. WHY: React will use index-based keys for this list, which can cause component state to be reused for the wrong rule when the filtered list reorders or updates, leading to incorrect actions/links being shown. HOW: Add `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport` on `isAlertingRule`, which is true only for alerting rules, whereas the ruler-based equivalent gated it on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` (true for all Grafana-managed rules). WHY: Grafana-managed recording rules lose the export action when viewed through the Prometheus-rule list path, breaking feature parity with the ruler-based view. HOW: Change the support flag to `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` or `true` for all Grafana-prom rules, e.g. `[prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), exportAllowed]`.

Producer/consumer mismatch for the silence action: GrafanaRuleListItem and GrafanaGroupLoader now render RuleActionsButtons with only a promRule and no rulerRule, but RuleActionsButtons.V2 still gates the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). When rule is undefined the drawer never opens, even though AlertRuleMenu computes canSilence from the promRule abilities and invokes handleSilence. The menu enables silence based on GrafanaPromRuleDTO, while the drawer consumer still requires a RulerRuleDTO. Align the drawer gating with the promRule-based abilities (or pass the rulerRule) so silence works from these call sites.

suggestions.label: potential issue
suggestions.suggestionContent: The key={promRule.uid} could be problematic if uids are not unique within a group, though this is noted as a pre-existing data contract issue.

suggestions.label: UX bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 104 uses rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) to decide whether to render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer. Since this component is now used with only promRule (no rule) from the list view, rule will be undefined; the guard evaluates false, so the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer won't open even when the silence action is triggered. This is a functional gap/UX bug and a possible regression for silencing from the list view.

suggestions.label: stray comment
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 289 has a stray `// duplicate` comment next to `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule)`; it appears to be a stray comment, not a code defect.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The silence drawer is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), which is false when only a Grafana PromRule is supplied. Now that the component is used with prom-only rules, clicking 'Silence notifications' opens state but the drawer never mounts. Render the drawer for Grafana-managed prom alerting rules as well, or provide a prom-rule-compatible silence path.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code maps over `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` without a fallback. If `groups` is empty, `at(0)` returns `undefined`, `?.rules` yields `undefined`, and `.map(...)` throws. The previous implementation guarded this with `?? []`. Restore the fallback: `(promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules ?? []).map(...)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The access-token ID matcher reads the wrong substring and inverts the equality check. WHY: The encoder writes the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 of the prefix, but the matcher reads substring(3, 5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut, so the matcher never rejects a token with the wrong grant type. HOW: Change the condition to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId is silently accepted, and the error message refers to grantType even though rawTokenId is the value being checked. HOW: Change the fourth requireNonNull to check rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `isAccessTokenId` matcher returns `false` when `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`. It should return `true` on a match. Fix the logic so the expected grant shortcut is required, not rejected. Also consider updating the misleading comment about the shortcut starting at the 4th character, since it is at 0-indexed positions 4-5.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The matcher extracts the grant-type shortcut from the wrong position. The encoder produces token ids as <sessionType:2><tokenType:2><grantType:2>:<rawId>, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 of the prefix, not 3-5. Change items[0].substring(3, 5) to items[0].substring(4, 6) and update the comment accordingly, otherwise valid token ids produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider will fail the assertion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The matcher checks items[0].substring(3, 5) to validate the 2-char grant shortcut, but the shortcut starts at index 4 and ends at index 6 in the 6-character prefix.
