This causes it to reject valid token IDs and to not actually verify the grant type. Change the check to substring(4, 6).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `isAccessTokenId` matcher extracts the wrong two-character grant-type segment and inverts the equality check. For the encoded token format `<st(2)><tt(2)><gt(2)>:<uuid>` the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 of the prefix, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`. The current `substring(3, 5)` reads the token-type/grant-type boundary, and the `if (...equals(...)) return false;` logic accepts non-matching grants and rejects matching ones. Fix the substring indices and use `!equals(...)` (or return true directly on match) so the matcher validates the expected grant type correctly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reader thread in the new test catches only Exception, so any Error (e.g., AssertionError, OutOfMemoryError) thrown during concurrent group reads is silently swallowed. WHY: The main thread then asserts caughtExceptions is empty and passes even though the reader thread failed, masking real failures and making the test give false confidence. HOW: Change the catch to Throwable, keep the exception list typed as Throwable, and use assertTrue(caughtThrowables.isEmpty(), ...) so any failure fails the test visibly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The test starts a background reader thread but never joins it before returning. WHY: The reader can continue executing groups() calls after the test method ends, during test cleanup or while the next test is running, causing potential flakiness and cross-test interference. HOW: Join the reader thread after setting deletedAll=true, with a reasonable timeout, and fail the test if it does not terminate.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reader thread is not joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, so exceptions caught after the assertion runs are missed and the test can falsely pass. Store the Thread reference and call thread.join() after deletedAll.set(true) before the assertThat check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test starts a reader thread but discards the Thread reference and never calls join(). After deletedAll.set(true) the main thread immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty, so the assertion may run before the reader thread records its final exception. The thread can also continue executing after the test method returns, potentially interfering with subsequent tests or cleanup. Capture the Thread and call thread.join() (handling InterruptedException) after deletedAll.set(true) and before the assertion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: getSubGroupsCount() changed from fail-fast to nullable when the underlying group is concurrently removed. Existing callers that unbox or dereference the result (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) will now throw NullPointerException instead of receiving a count. Either return a safe default such as 0L, or audit and update every consumer to handle null.

suggestions.label: null-safety
suggestions.suggestionContent: getSubGroupsStream (lines 262, 268) still calls modelSupplier.get().method() without null checks. This pre-existing null-safety gap is not modified by this PR and is out of scope for the cross-file analysis.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The HTML tag detector and anchor matcher use case-sensitive regular expressions (`<[a-z]+[^>]*>` and `]*>`) even though HTML element names are case-insensitive. WHY: The OWASP sanitizer canonicalizes tag names to lowercase, so a translation with `text` or `` is not matched by the anchor pre-check and is then normalized by the sanitizer to lowercase, making `sanitized != value` and causing a false-positive "Illegal HTML" build failure. HOW: Compile `HTML_TAGS` and `ANCHOR_PATTERN` with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (or add `A-Z` to the character classes for tags and `A` for anchors) so the verifier treats HTML case-insensitively.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `verifySafeHtml` unconditionally throws `RuntimeException` when the computed English base file cannot be read. WHY: Any community translation file that does not have a matching `_en.properties` in the parallel `resources` directory will cause a `FileNotFoundException`, which is wrapped in `RuntimeException` and aborts the entire Maven build instead of reporting a verification message. HOW: Treat a missing English base as a verification message (e.g., "Missing English base file for ...") or fall back to an empty bundle, rather than throwing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The diff-prefix/suffix stripping at lines 101-111 can compute start >= value.length() - end (for example when a single character is sanitized in the middle, or when the entire value is changed). Calling value.substring(start, value.length() - end) with beginIndex > endIndex throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, turning an HTML validation failure into a build crash. Clamp the indices so that the substring is never inverted, e.g. ensure endIndex = Math.max(start, value.length() - end) and similarly for sanitized.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The newly added private method is named `santizeAnchors` (line 88 and 150) but it clearly performs anchor sanitization. The rest of the file uses the correct spelling `sanitize` (e.g. `verifySafeHtml`, `policy.sanitize`, `sanitized`). Rename the method to `sanitizeAnchors` so the identifier matches its documented purpose and surrounding naming conventions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `loginTotpStep1` message in the Lithuanian locale was changed to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This breaks localization because the file is for Lithuanian users. Restore a proper Lithuanian translation that matches the new English source text.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `totpStep1` message in the Lithuanian account messages file was changed to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This is a localization defect in a Lithuanian resource bundle. It should be translated into Lithuanian.

suggestions.label: info
suggestions.suggestionContent: New error/reporting paths in verifySafeHtml() include java.io.File instances (file/englishFile) whose toString() yields absolute paths, so build logs will contain absolute filesystem paths. This occurs at lines 70 and 79 (RuntimeException with file/englishFile) and line 111 (messages.add with file). This is minor information disclosure, but it is already present in unchanged code at line 53 (MojoExecutionException with file) and is standard output for Maven plugins; the PR does not introduce a new class of sensitive-data exposure. No data-exposure defect of the assigned class is present. Note: line 157 (messages.add with matcher.group()) echoes anchor tags, which is expected behavior for a verifier and does not constitute disclosure of sensitive data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: verifySafeHtml() wraps I/O failures in RuntimeException, which escapes verify()'s IOException catch block and crashes the Maven plugin instead of producing a controlled MojoExecutionException. Change the catch blocks to throw MojoExecutionException (or let the IOException propagate so verify() handles it).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Replace the FileInputStream-based PropertyResourceBundle construction with UTF-8 Reader-based construction. The existing verify() path uses Files.readString (UTF-8), but PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) decodes as ISO-8859-1, so the HTML verifier interprets the same file differently than the duplicate-key verifier. This corrupts UTF-8 translations (e.g., the modified Chinese properties files) and can produce incorrect 'Illegal HTML' results or garbled error messages. Use Files.newBufferedReader(file.toPath(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8) for both bundle reads.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The provider event listener that disables permissions on role/client/group removal now runs only when the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. WHY: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is independent (it depends only on AUTHORIZATION), so in V2-only deployments the listener is skipped and stale permissions remain after resources are deleted, breaking the invariant that permissions disappear with their target. HOW: Change the guard to check both features, e.g. `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) || Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` do not verify that returned `Permission.resourceId` matches the resource being evaluated. WHY: If `root.evaluatePermission` returns permissions for other resources (e.g. a different client or the all-clients resource), the loops will grant access based solely on matching scopes, allowing a permission meant for one client to satisfy a check for another. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission filters on `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`, so the same defensive check should be applied here. HOW: Add the resourceId equality guard inside the permission loops in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission`.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `getClientsWithPermission(String)` loads every client resource of type Clients and evaluates permissions for each one. WHY: For realms with many clients this produces O(N) authorization evaluations on every caller such as `AvailableRoleMappingResource`, causing linear slowdown of role-mapping and client-listing operations. HOW: Consider evaluating a single all-clients resource first and returning early when a global grant exists; otherwise keep per-client evaluation but bound it with pagination or cache granted scopes per request.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.', but the method signature is 'void requireView();'. This contradicts the actual contract and should be corrected to 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}.' to match the pattern used by the neighbouring require* methods.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.', but the method signature is 'void requireViewClientScopes();'. The prose should be updated to 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code false}.' to reflect the actual API contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Javadoc says 'Or if the caller has a permission to {@link AdminPermissionManagement#VIEW_SCOPE} the client. For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to {@link org.keycloak.authorization.AdminPermissionsSchema#VIEW} all clients.' However, ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) only checks canView()/canConfigure(client) and AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW; it never evaluates AdminPermissionManagement.VIEW_SCOPE. The 'Also' wording is misleading because the V1 per-client check is absent in V2.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, even though these methods are part of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface contract. Since MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, callers holding a ClientPermissionEvaluator reference that invoke these methods will break. Either provide a V2 implementation that honors the interface contract, add default no-op behavior to the interface, or update all consumers to avoid calling these methods on V2.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tests call getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) and .get(0) without checking that the list contains enough elements. If the realm has fewer default scopes than assumed, the test throws IndexOutOfBoundsException before it can verify the intended ForbiddenException behavior. Guard the index access with an isEmpty()/size() check or select a scope safely, and fail with a clear message if none are available.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), but in the V2 permission path clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, deleting a client will therefore raise an unhandled exception and abort the transaction. The cleanup should either be skipped for V2, or ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled should be a no-op (or properly clean up V2 authorization resources).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In V2 there is no per-client permission toggle, but the client-removal cleanup path in AdminPermissions.java still invokes setPermissionsEnabled(...). Make this method a no-op instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client does not fail when admin fine-grained authz V2 is enabled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Javadoc/comment for USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH still describes the previous behavior of preventing user clearing on failed password authentication. After the refactor the flag is consumed only by AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to hide the username and disable registration during re-authentication. The comment should be updated to match the current observable effect, otherwise future maintainers will look for user-clearing logic that is no longer governed by this flag.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The test cleanup references the literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias. WHY: Created identity providers are never removed after the test, leaking state into subsequent tests and the test realm. HOW: Use the actual alias variable in the cleanup closure, e.g. testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove and testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The second cleanup in the same test method also references the literal string "alias" instead of "idp-alias-20". WHY: The identity provider created for the invalidation scenario is not removed, leaving stale test data behind. HOW: Change the cleanup to reference the actual alias: testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: remove(String) now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally before the existing cache branch. WHY: The delegate database query previously only ran when the alias cache entry was already invalid; it now runs on every IDP removal, adding a redundant round-trip. HOW: Keep the delegate lookup inside the invalidation branch, or derive the login-cache invalidation from the CachedIdentityProvider already fetched in the else branch when present.

suggestions.label: test-quality
suggestions.suggestionContent: The added test testCacheIDPForLogin validates implementation details (exact cache-key presence/absence after create/update/remove operations) rather than externally observable behavior. This soft concern does not cause the test to pass when the behavior is broken, but the test remains coupled to internal cache keys instead of public behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cleanup lambda references the literal alias "alias" instead of the IDP's real alias "idp-alias-" + i that was just set on idpRep. As a result the cleanup will fail to remove the created provider and may throw, leaving test data behind. Use the actual alias variable or inline the computed alias in the cleanup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cleanup lambda again references the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias "idp-alias-20". The cleanup will not remove the provider created in this block. Use "idp-alias-20" in the cleanup reference.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty columns and empty data when the use-table-widget-visualization feature is enabled. WHY: Widgets with real table results display a blank table instead of the fetched data, breaking the dashboard table visualization for that feature. HOW: Pass the actual fields/result data (e.g., result.data, result.meta, widget.queries[i]?.fields) into TableWidgetVisualization instead of the placeholder values.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: BrowserReportSerializer makes both age and timestamp optional without requiring at least one, and the cross-field validation messages are swapped. WHY: A report can pass validation with neither age nor timestamp, violating both Reporting API specs, and the returned errors point the caller to the wrong field. HOW: Add serializer-level validate() that ensures exactly one of age/timestamp is present, and fix the messages so the timestamp validator complains about age and vice versa.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results by relying on dict insertion order via zip(error_ids, events.values()). WHY: If the nodestore backend returns results in a different order, omits missing keys, or if any error_id maps to None, the returned ErrorEvent id can be attached to the wrong event data. HOW: Iterate over node_ids and lookup each node_id in the events dict, then map back to the original event_id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: get_request_data sorts the error_events list in place. WHY: Callers that reuse the error_events list after calling get_request_data will see it reordered, which is an unexpected side effect and can break downstream logic. HOW: Sort a copy of the list instead of mutating the input.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: get_environment_info catches the base Exception class and silently continues. WHY: Real failures (e.g., database or nodestore errors) are swallowed and hidden from monitoring, making debugging impossible and potentially masking data corruption. HOW: Catch only the specific exceptions that indicate a missing environment, and send actual infrastructure errors to sentry_sdk instead of logging at info.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The endpoint logs the entire request body (`request.data`) at info level and logs each raw report on validation failure. Browser reports include `url`, `user_agent`, and arbitrary report bodies that can contain page URLs, source file paths, and other browsing context. This exposes potentially sensitive data to logs. Redact or omit the request body/raw report from log messages, and log only non-sensitive identifiers such as report type and validation error category.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` methods check for the presence of the opposite field with `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is a valid integer value for both fields but is falsy, a report containing `timestamp: 0` with an `age`, or `age: 0` with a `timestamp`, will incorrectly pass validation. Use explicit existence checks such as `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead of relying on truthiness.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `_truncate_title` returns `title[:max_length].rstrip() + "..."` when the title exceeds `max_length`. For a 51-character title this yields 50 characters plus 3 ellipsis characters (53 total), exceeding the intended `ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` of 50. Either reserve room for the ellipsis before slicing (e.g., slice to `max_length - 3`) or ensure the final string is clamped to `max_length`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: submit() sums Redis cluster memory info once per flusher process. WHY: iter_cluster_memory_usage returns per-master-node usage for the shared Redis cluster, so summing across N buffers inflates used/available by N and can falsely trigger the hard backpressure pause. HOW: collect memory_info from a single buffer (e.g. next(iter(self.buffers.values())).get_memory_info()) instead of extending across all buffers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: _ensure_processes_alive() checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) before killing a process. WHY: the flusher uses multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), whose Process class is multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, not multiprocessing.Process (fork on Linux), so the guard is False and dead/hung child processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, leaking processes. HOW: kill any non-thread process, e.g. check not isinstance(process, threading.Thread) or use hasattr(process, "kill").

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: join() breaks out of the per-process loop as soon as the deadline expires for one process. WHY: remaining later processes are not waited for or terminated, so they can keep running past the shutdown timeout and leak. HOW: continue to the next process instead of break, or at least terminate each process before moving on.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the implementation on lines 60-66 creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes and assigns multiple shards to each process via modulo. When `max_processes` is less than the shard count, shards share processes, which the new test verifies (4 shards, 2 processes). The docstring should be updated to describe the actual process-per-shard-group behavior, e.g. "Creates up to `max_processes` processes and distributes shards across them."

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: At line 51, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses truthiness to decide whether a value was supplied. A caller can explicitly pass `flusher_processes=0`, but it will be ignored and replaced with the shard count. Use an explicit None check: `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 is meant to give flusher threads/processes time to process after advancing the drift, but `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to a no-op at line 15. The call returns immediately, so the test does not actually wait for the condition it claims to synchronize on. Replace the fixed sleep with a proper condition (e.g., wait on the flusher state, or use a short polling loop with a real timeout) and only patch `time.sleep` inside the flusher code if you need to speed up its internal loop.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The flusher explicitly uses spawn context (`multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`) and annotates processes as `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, but the kill guard checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. On Linux `multiprocessing.Process` is `ForkProcess`, so the check is False for `SpawnProcess`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` will not kill a hung flusher before creating a replacement. Use a check that covers the actual process type, e.g. `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` tag the shard list with key `"shard"`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` tags the same `shard_tag` value with key `"shards"`. Queries and dashboards will not see all three metrics for the same shard filter. Pick one key (e.g. `"shard"`) and use it consistently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `queued` default uses `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default, which evaluates once at class definition time. WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value will share the same stale datetime (when the module was first imported), defeating the purpose of recording when the assignment was queued. HOW: Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets a fresh timestamp at creation time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: AssignmentSource.to_dict() returns a dataclass.asdict() that includes a datetime object in the `queued` field. This dict is passed through apply_async kwargs and serialized by Celery using JSON, which cannot encode datetime. The task will fail at the serialization boundary with a TypeError. Serialize `queued` to an ISO 8601 string in to_dict and parse it back in from_dict so the payload is JSON-safe.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test `test_from_dict_empty_array` is misnamed because it passes an empty dictionary (`{}`), not an empty array. Rename it to `test_from_dict_empty_dict` so the test name accurately describes the scenario it covers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: test_from_dict_empty_array is named to exercise from_dict with an empty array, but the body passes an empty dict ({}). If from_dict([]) behaved incorrectly (e.g., raised instead of returning None), this test would still pass because it never uses []. Rename the test to test_from_dict_empty_dict or change the input to [] to match the name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: test_from_dict_inalid_data contains a typo (inalid instead of invalid). This means the test is skipped when developers or CI filter tests by name (e.g., pytest -k invalid), so the invalid-data handling it covers would not be exercised in those runs. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The task was updated to pass `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`, but the abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` and concrete integration implementations were not updated to accept that parameter. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new user-mismatch check reads integration.metadata['sender']['login'] without verifying that the 'sender' key exists. WHY: Integrations that pre-date this metadata field or were created without the installation webhook will raise KeyError and crash the installation pipeline instead of showing the intended error page. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `error_short` strings (`"Invalid installation request."`, `"GitHub installation pending deletion."`, `"Github installed on another Sentry organization."`) are user-facing messages, but they are passed as plain string literals to `error()` rather than being wrapped in `_()`. suggestions.label: bug

WHY: Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self) at runtime; any detector whose type maps to MetricAlertFire will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. HOW: Add stub implementations for the abstract methods (raising NotImplementedError where behavior is still TODO) so the class remains instantiable while the stateful abstraction is being built.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says 'within the threshold of commits' but the surrounding code filters MonitorCheckIns. The word 'commits' is a leftover/copy-paste error and disagrees with the code; it should say 'check-ins'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The issue_title, subtitle, evidence display names ('Failure reason', 'Environment', 'Last successful check-in'), and the fallback value 'Never' are hard-coded English strings that reach the user. Other strings in this file use gettext_lazy (`_()`). Wrap these UI strings with `_()` so they can be localized consistently with the rest of the failure evidence.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The docstring examples include 'A failed check-in was detected', but the function returns status-specific singular messages such as 'An error check-in was detected' and there is no CheckInStatus.FAILED. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its display name, but then returns the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified `config` copy. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: checkIfIsAvailable returns true as soon as it finds a matching date override, before checking the host's busy times. WHY: A fixed host with a conflicting booking during an override window is still considered available, so round-robin/collective slots can be double-booked. HOW: Move the date-override validation into the existing `busy.every` check or keep the override guard but still evaluate `busy` before returning true.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The working-hours guard sets `end` to the same minute-of-day value as `start` (lines 141-142). WHY: Slots that start within working hours but run past the host's end time are accepted, letting a host be booked outside their availability. HOW: Compute `end` from `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The all-day-unavailable override check compares two dayjs objects with `===` (line 114). WHY: Each `dayjs(...)` call returns a new object, so the comparison is always false and a same-start/end override is treated as a normal availability window instead of blocking the whole day. HOW: Use `.isSame()` to compare the two moments.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Date-override comparisons in checkIfIsAvailable format dayjs objects that were constructed from a Date without forcing UTC mode (lines 110-111, 114, 118, 123). WHY: Because the dayjs default is not pinned to UTC, the formatted day/hour depends on the server's local timezone, so the override may match the wrong UTC slot or not match at all. HOW: Parse and format the override dates in UTC: `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` and use `.utc()` consistently for comparisons.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test at lines 788-804 asserts only the final UTC time slots, with a comment claiming 'it should return the same as this is the utc time'. Because UTC slot strings are compared against themselves, the test would still pass if the date-override timezone conversion were removed or broken. To make the test meaningful, compare the slots produced with the invitee timezone against the slots produced with a neutral/UTC invitee timezone (or directly verify the override's local boundaries are converted correctly), so a regression in the timezone offset math causes a mismatch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 114 uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two distinct `dayjs(...)` instances. Because each `dayjs()` call returns a new object, the comparison always fails even when the dates are equal. This causes zero-length date overrides not to be treated as unavailable. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare Unix timestamps/ISO strings instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Lines 141-142 compute `start` and `end` from the same `slotStartTime`, so `end` never reflects `slotEndTime`. The subsequent check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore cannot reject a slot that starts within working hours but ends after them. Change `end` to `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `checkIfIsAvailable` function was changed to also validate `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`, but the call inside the `selectedSlots` block only passes `busy` and `...availabilityCheckProps`. Since `availabilityCheckProps` only contains `eventLength` and `currentSeats`, the new date-override and working-hours checks are skipped for this re-filtering pass. Pass `...userSchedule` (or explicitly include `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`) so the consumer matches the updated contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Each date override now carries its own `timeZone` (added in the same PR at lines 411-415 and used by `packages/lib/slots.ts` at lines 211-225), but `checkIfIsAvailable` ignores that field and converts every override with the single `organizerTimeZone` argument. For multi-host events this can map an override to the wrong UTC day. Use `date.timeZone` (falling back to `organizerTimeZone` only when absent) inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback when formatting/comparing `date.start` and `date.end`, and update the `dateOverrides` parameter type to include `timeZone?: string`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `forEach` callback was changed to async, but `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`. WHY: Errors that were previously caught synchronously now become unhandled promise rejections, bypassing the logger and potentially crashing the process. HOW: Replace `forEach(async …)` with `for…of` and await each operation inside the loop.

WHY: Errors that were previously caught synchronously now become unhandled promise rejections, bypassing the logger and potentially crashing the process. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `forEach` callback was changed to async so `getCalendar` could be awaited, but `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, and `deleteMeeting` escape tRPC's error handling. WHY: Errors that previously propagated synchronously to the tRPC handler now become unhandled promise rejections, and the cancellation operations are fire-and-forget. HOW: Replace `forEach(async …)` with `for…of` and await each operation, or collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all(...)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: getCalendarCredentials remains synchronous but calls the now-async getCalendar, so the returned calendar field is a Promise instead of a Calendar. This changes the contract of the exported helper. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar(credential) so the shape of the returned objects stays the same (only the function itself becomes async), or explicitly document and verify every consumer awaits item.calendar.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Converting the forEach callback to async makes the returned promises fire-and-forget: rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent are unhandled and the caller cannot await completion. Replace with Promise.all(map(...)) and await each operation so errors propagate and deletions complete before proceeding.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Same as the vital reschedule path: the async forEach callback ignores the promises it returns, so getCalendar or deleteEvent failures become unhandled rejections and the operation may not finish before the handler returns. Use Promise.all(map(...)) and await each step.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The async forEach callback means the surrounding code does not wait for the recurring-booking calendar updates, and any rejection from getCalendar or updateEvent is unhandled. Replace with a for...of loop so updates are awaited and errors propagate.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The async callback passed to forEach returns a promise that forEach ignores. Rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent become unhandled, and the router cannot guarantee the deletion completes before responding. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: When a booking is rescheduled via handleNewBooking.ts, the previous booking's email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true and the booking is kept, so the stale rows remain in the database until their scheduledDate passes; the cron only cleans cancelled=true rows, causing a reminder row leak. HOW: Delete the row after the SendGrid cancel request in the immediateDelete branch.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The remindersToCancel loop awaits each SendGrid cancel request sequentially. WHY: Each cancelled reminder within the next hour triggers a separate blocking network round-trip, so cancellation latency grows linearly with the number of cancelled reminders and can delay the cron run. HOW: Collect the client.request promises and await Promise.all, or use a bounded concurrency helper like async.mapLimit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The function deleteScheduledEmailReminder now, by default, only sets `cancelled: true` on the row and does not delete it, while its name and the callers' expectations (e.g., 'deleteScheduledEmailReminder') say it deletes the reminder. Rename it to something like cancelScheduledEmailReminder or split the 'mark cancelled' and 'delete' paths so the name matches the behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `referenceId` is present and `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled: true`. Because the cleanup cron only processes rows with `cancelled: true`, these reminders are never removed from the database. For callers that are not followed by a cascade delete (e.g. rescheduling in `handleNewBooking.ts`), this leaks stale rows. The `immediateDelete` branch should either delete the row directly (matching `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) or mark it `cancelled: true` so the cron can remove it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The call to SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId passes an empty data object, which Prisma treats as a no-op. WHY: With data: {}, Prisma performs no actual column writes, so the @updatedAt timestamp on SelectedCalendar is not refreshed and the cache-status UI continues to show a stale 'last updated' time. HOW: Pass { updatedAt: new Date() } in the data argument so the timestamp is explicitly updated.

WHY: The factory checks the 'calendar-cache' feature flag globally and returns a no-op mock when disabled; bypassing it forces a calendarCache.groupBy query on every settings-page load even for tenants that have the feature turned off. suggestions.suggestionContent: The new updateManyByCredentialId method passes `data` directly to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. Its caller in CalendarService.ts invokes it with `{}` to bump `updatedAt`, but Prisma's updateMany requires at least one field in `data`; an empty object causes a Prisma Client validation error and breaks the availability refresh. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but an empty `data` object does not change any columns and therefore will not trigger Prisma's `@updatedAt` (and may throw). suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a case-sensitive lookup on the supplied email. WHY: An attacker can bypass a block for foo@example.com by signing up with FOO@EXAMPLE.COM, because the WHERE clause and stored value are not normalized to the same case. HOW: Downcase the email before storing and before looking it up, e.g. BlockedEmail.where(email: email.downcase).first and self.email = email.downcase in set_defaults or a before_validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? calls value =~ regexp without guarding against nil. WHY: When a record has a nil email and email_changed? is true, validate_each raises NoMethodError instead of adding a clean validation error. This also makes the validator unsafe for reuse on any model without a presence validation. HOW: Return early when value is blank, e.g. return if value.blank? at the start of validate_each or email_in_restriction_setting?.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? reads match_count, increments it in memory, and saves, creating a read-modify-write race. WHY: Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email load the same counter, increment, and save; one save clobbers the other, under-counting blocks and producing incorrect last_match_at. HOW: Update the counters atomically with update_all, e.g. BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now]).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `should_block?` method queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` and the client later checks `rejectedEmails.contains(email)`. Email addresses are case-insensitive identifiers; a record stored as `bad@example.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Bad@Example.com`. Normalize the address to lower case before both lookups (and store blocked emails in lower case), or use a case-insensitive query, to prevent case-sensitivity bypass.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `email_in_restriction_setting?` builds `/@(#{domains})/i` without anchoring the end of the address. A whitelist/blacklist entry like `example.com` will match `attacker@example.com.evil.tld` because `@example.com` appears inside the address. Anchor the match to the end of the value, e.g. `/@(#{domains})\z/i`, and ensure the value is normalized for case consistency.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact case-sensitive match, but email addresses are normally treated as case-insensitive. Normalize the lookup value (and the stored value) to lowercase, or use a case-insensitive query, so that `Bad@SpamClub.com` is blocked when `bad@spamclub.com` is in the blocked list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When an email is in `rejectedEmails`, `emailMatch` always returns `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. The server, however, returns distinct `user.email.not_allowed` and `user.email.blocked` messages in `result.errors.email`. The client should preserve and display the server's actual rejection reason, or at least distinguish blocked emails, instead of collapsing every server rejection into the generic 'invalid' message.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tests stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?` with Mocha `stubs`, which does not require the method to be invoked, and the positive case only asserts that some email error exists. If the blocked-email branch in EmailValidator were deleted, the first test would still pass; the second could pass from the whitelist/blacklist branch if SiteSetting is configured. Switch to `expects(:should_block?).with(record.email)` to force the call, stub `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` and `email_domains_blacklist` to empty strings, and assert the exact blocked-email error message (e.g. `should include I18n.t(:'user.email.blocked')`) so the tests actually fail when the behaviour they name is broken.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: should_block? reads the blocked email record, increments match_count in memory, and then calls save. Under concurrent requests with the same blocked email, two threads can read the same match_count, both compute the same incremented value, and both save, so one update is lost. Use an atomic single-statement update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now]) instead of the read-modify-save pattern.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The server now returns a structured `errors` hash (introduced in users_controller.rb:198) that can include email errors for several reasons: blocked email, disallowed domain, or already-taken uniqueness. The controller was updated to read `result.errors.email`, but it pushes the address into `rejectedEmails` for any email error and later shows `user.email.invalid`. This conflates "already taken" with "invalid/blocked" and prevents the user from re-submitting an address they might need to log into instead. The consumer should inspect the error key/message (e.g., distinguish `user.email.blocked`/`not_allowed` from the uniqueness error) before treating the email as permanently rejected.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has never viewed the topic, and the code immediately calls tu.notification_level. WHY: A logged-in user with no topic_user row (e.g., a category watcher clicking the email unsubscribe link) triggers a NoMethodError instead of being unsubscribed. HOW: Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level) instead of find_by/save!, which creates the row when absent and keeps notification reason/MessageBus behavior consistent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: @topic_view is instantiated before TopicUser is modified, and TopicView.topic_user is memoized, so perform_show_response serializes the old notification_level. WHY: The user sees the pre-unsubscribe notification state on the page after clicking unsubscribe, making the action appear to have failed. HOW: Re-instantiate @topic_view after updating the notification level (or clear its @topic_user cache) before calling perform_show_response.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (e.g. a user who has never viewed the topic follows the email unsubscribe link). The code then calls `tu.notification_level` unconditionally, which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`, resulting in a 500 error instead of a useful unsubscribe page. Either create a TopicUser record when missing, or guard against nil and render an appropriate message.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: TopicUser.find_by can return nil if the user has no existing TopicUser record for the topic. The code then calls tu.notification_level unconditionally, which will raise NoMethodError. Add a guard or create a TopicUser before reading notification_level.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by result without checking for nil. If the user has no TopicUser record for the topic, the action crashes with NoMethodError on tu.notification_level instead of creating a muted record or downgrading the level. Add a guard to create or handle a nil TopicUser before reading notification_level.

suggestions.label: authorization
suggestions.suggestionContent: `Topic#unsubscribe_url` returns `#{url}/unsubscribe`, a public URL path with no sensitive token or secret. Because visiting this URL automatically changes the recipient's notification level without requiring any authentication token, the URL acts as a capability-bearing link: if forwarded or logged, anyone with the link can alter the user's notification state. The reviewer classifies this as an authorization/CSRF-like issue rather than data exposure, so it is noted but not reported under the data-exposure class.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR adds topic-specific unsubscribe_url support and updates the builder spec to pass unsubscribe_url, but the tests in the 'with add_unsubscribe_link true' context only check the List-Unsubscribe header and the user_preferences_url in the body. They do not verify that unsubscribe_url is interpolated into the unsubscribe link or body. Add an assertion that message_with_unsubscribe.body contains the provided unsubscribe_url (or that the cooked unsubscribe_link includes it), otherwise the new behavior is untested and could be broken without failing the suite.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The stopNotificiationsText property interpolates model.fancyTitle directly into an I18n string and the unsubscribe.hbs template renders it with triple braces ({{{...}}}). The locale string wraps the title in <strong>, but because triple braces bypass Ember HTML escaping, any HTML/JS in the topic title will be executed in the user's browser. If fancyTitle is not guaranteed to be escaped server-side, this is an XSS vulnerability. Either escape the title before interpolation (e.g. Handlebars.Utils.escapeExpression) or render the locale HTML wrapper around an escaped {{title}} instead of using triple braces for the whole sentence.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` is a relative path, but it is passed to the email builder where it becomes a link in an email. Email links must be absolute. Prepend `Discourse.base_url` here (consistent with how `user_preferences_url` is built and how `post.url` is used in the same template), e.g. `unsubscribe_url: "#{Discourse.base_url}#{post.topic.unsubscribe_url}"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The light-theme argument for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. WHY: On light themes the author link becomes much lighter than intended, breaking the muted style and lowering contrast. HOW: Keep the first argument at 30% and use 70% only for the secondary dark-theme argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The light-theme value for `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. WHY: The name renders lighter/less bold than the original design on light themes. HOW: Restore the first argument to 30% and use 70% for the secondary dark-theme argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The light-theme value for `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. WHY: The mobile name renders lighter than intended and no longer matches the desktop style. HOW: Restore the first argument to 30% and use 70% for the secondary dark-theme argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `.topic-map h3` on mobile changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for light themes. WHY: It becomes too light and no longer matches the desktop topic map heading, which keeps 20%/80%. HOW: Use 20% for the primary light-theme argument and 80% for the secondary dark-theme argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `.custom-message-length` on mobile changed the light-theme value from 70% to 30% and the dark-theme value from 30% to 70%, opposite of the desktop modal. WHY: The hint becomes much darker than intended on light themes and is inconsistent with the desktop modal. HOW: Match the desktop modal by using 70% primary for light themes and 30% secondary for dark themes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `.topic-meta-data h5 a` rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement passes `70%` as the light-scheme argument and `30%` as the dark-scheme argument, which is backwards: in the light scheme the link becomes much lighter than intended, and in the dark scheme it becomes too dark. The first argument should preserve the original `30%` and the second should be `70%` to maintain the same muted appearance on a dark background.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The mobile `.custom-message-length` rule now uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for light schemes and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark schemes. The desktop equivalent (desktop/modal.scss:50) keeps the original `70%` for light schemes and `30%` for dark schemes. These two implementations disagree, so the mobile hint will be too dark in light mode and too light in dark mode.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The mobile onebox `h3` color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(...50%, ...50%)`, while the desktop onebox `h3` (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) preserves `20%` for light schemes and uses `80%` for dark schemes. The mobile version both alters the light-scheme appearance and produces a different dark-scheme shade than desktop, breaking visual parity across viewports.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The conditional inclusion method for `website_name` is named `include_website_name` without the required trailing `?`, so ActiveModelSerializers 0.8 ignores it. WHY: `website_name` is always serialized, bypassing the `untrusted_attributes` guard on `website` and exposing the user's website host/path to anonymous/TL0 viewers even when `website` is hidden. HOW: Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and mirror the `website` guard: `def include_website_name?; return false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object); website.present?; end`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The method is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModel::Serializers invokes `include_website_name?` to decide whether to serialize the attribute. Rename it to `include_website_name?` so the intended guard actually runs, otherwise `website_name` is always included regardless of whether the user has a website.

suggestions.label: error-handling
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `website_name` method parses the serialized `website` value using `URI(...).host` and `URI(...).path`, and the `rescue nil` swallows parse errors silently without logging the URL or the error, making failures undiagnosable.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Domain names are case-insensitive, but website_name compares URI(website).host against Discourse.current_hostname using case-sensitive ==, ends_with?, and split/join comparisons. Normalize both hosts (e.g., downcase) before comparing so that http://EXAMPLE.COM/... on an instance at example.com is recognized as the same domain and the path logic is not bypassed by case variation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `applyTemplateVariables` does not inject `datasource: this.getRef()` onto each query, while the previous `interpolateVariablesInQueries` did. WHY: Downstream consumers of `runSplitQuery` that expect each target to carry its `datasource` reference may receive queries without it, breaking mixed-datasource requests or any code that reads `target.datasource`. HOW: Either call `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)` which preserves the reference, or map the result of `applyTemplateVariables` to add `datasource: datasource.getRef()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new code filters hidden targets and empty expressions before applying template variables, while the old `interpolateVariablesInQueries` call interpolated the entire target list first. WHY: Hidden targets that contain template variables are no longer expanded, which can change side effects (e.g., variable dependency tracking, ad-hoc filter application) and may leave variables unexpanded if a target is later un-hidden or inspected. HOW: Interpolate variables before filtering, or keep the same order as the old implementation: `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars, request.filters).filter(...)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false, ignoring the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. WHY: Operators who enable the feature flag still cannot use SQL expressions, and the feature-flag check is dead code that contradicts its name. HOW: Either return the flag value (`return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`) if SQL should remain toggleable, or make the kill-switch explicit by returning `false` and removing the unused parameter/import.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag it checks and always returns false. The function computes whether FlagSqlExpressions is NOT enabled, then returns false in both branches, so SQL expressions are rejected even when the flag is turned on. It should return the actual flag state, e.g. `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Replacing the real in-memory DB with a stub means `sql.TablesList(rawSQL)` always fails, so the existing `logger.Warn("invalid sql query", "sql", rawSQL, "error", err)` at lines 32-35 now logs the full raw SQL for every SQL expression. User-supplied SQL can contain sensitive values or schema information and should not be logged verbatim. Avoid logging `rawSQL` or redact it before logging.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The helper unconditionally returns false because it negates the flag and then returns false in both branches. This makes SQL expressions permanently disabled, ignoring FlagSqlExpressions. Return the actual flag value instead of negating it and short-circuiting to false.

The enableSqlExpressions logic contains suspicious always-false logic that is a functional/feature-flag bug (the reviewer notes this is outside the assigned secrets/identity/comparisons/crypto class).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `enableSqlExpressions` function is named to indicate it returns whether SQL expressions should be enabled, but it always returns `false`. It assigns `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches, so the feature flag is effectively ignored and callers always see the "not implemented" path. The implementation should return the actual feature-flag state (e.g. `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`) so the function name matches its behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `enableSqlExpressions` helper is logically inverted/buggy: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns `false` in both branches. As a result, `ReadQuery` rejects every SQL expression with "sqlExpressions is not implemented", even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is globally enabled. The function should return the actual enabled state of the flag (or at least return `true` when the flag is enabled) so the feature gate matches its intended contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `NewInMemoryDB()` now returns a `DB` whose `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` always return "not implemented". This changes the behavior contract from the previous real DuckDB implementation. Callers such as `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:TablesList` and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go:Execute` were updated to use the local symbol but still depend on it actually parsing SQL and running queries, so SQL expressions will always fail. Either restore a working implementation or update every consumer to handle the permanent failure explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: NewInMemoryDB returns a DB whose methods always return "not implemented". pkg/expr/sql/parser.go and pkg/expr/sql_command.go call these methods expecting real SQL parsing and execution, so SQL expressions will always fail. Either implement the methods or update callers to match the stub contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The denial cache key concatenates resource name and parent folder using `_` separators without escaping them. WHY: A resource named `x_y` inside folder `z` produces the same key as a resource named `x` inside folder `y_z`, so a denial for one resource can be incorrectly returned for the other. HOW: Encode or escape underscores in `name` and `parent` before building the key, or use a structured key format (e.g., JSON/protobuf) that cannot collide.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The denial cache stores negative authorization decisions for `shortCacheTTL` (30 seconds) and is never invalidated. WHY: If a user is denied access, then an admin grants permission to that exact resource, subsequent Check calls hit the cached denial and return false until the TTL expires, contradicting the PR goal of letting users access newly authorized dashboards and folders. HOW: Invalidate the matching denial cache entry whenever the user's permissions for the action are refreshed or updated; alternatively, skip denial caching for wildcard-capable actions or reduce the TTL if invalidation is not feasible.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When permissions are found in the permission cache but `checkPermission` returns false, the code increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label `false` as if the cache missed. WHY: This metric conflates actual cache misses with cache hits that did not grant access, making cache-hit observability inaccurate. HOW: Increment the cache-usage metric with `true` immediately after a successful `getCachedIdentityPermissions` return, before evaluating whether the permission grants access.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with only underscores as separators. Grafana folder/dashboard UIDs can contain underscores, so different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key (e.g. name="a_b", parent="c" vs name="a", parent="b_c"). A collision makes the denial cache return a false denial for a different resource. Use an unambiguous encoding such as null-byte delimiters or a hash of the components.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Check consults permDenialCache before the permission cache and DB, and only writes to it when the DB lookup denies. If a user's permissions change from deny to allow, the stale denial entry remains for the cache TTL and continues to deny access even though the current permission set would grant it. Either delete the denial entry when a Check finally allows, or avoid negative caching in the authorization path.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The background cleanup ticker now fires every minute instead of every ten minutes. WHY: Each cleanup run uses a 9-minute timeout, so the shorter interval allows overlapping runs, increases database load, and can reintroduce the concurrency problems the PR is trying to solve. HOW: Restore the 10-minute interval unless the change is intentional and the timeout is adjusted accordingly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cleanup code logs every batch of annotation/tag IDs and counts at Error level during normal operation. WHY: This generates false error alerts and writes large ID slices to logs on each batch, increasing log volume and noise. HOW: Use Debug or Info level and log only the count (and optionally a sample of IDs) instead of the full slice.

suggestions.label: logging-level-misuse
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the MaxAge cleanup fetch-then-delete loop (lines 523-538), the log statements "Annotations to clean by time" and "cleaned annotations by time" are emitted at Error level even though they fire on every successful batch of normal operation. Error logs are meant to signal failures, so logging normal cleanup activity at Error level makes monitoring/alerting on errors incorrect. This is a measurement/naming issue — these messages should not be logged at Error level.

suggestions.label: logging-level-misuse
suggestions.suggestionContent: The same Error-level logging pattern repeats for the MaxCount cleanup loop (lines 547-558): normal successful operation is logged at Error level, which is incorrect for monitoring/alerting purposes and should be changed to a non-error level.

suggestions.label: logging-level-misuse
suggestions.suggestionContent: The same Error-level logging pattern also repeats for the orphaned-tags cleanup (lines 569-580): normal successful operation is logged at Error level, which is incorrect for monitoring/alerting purposes and should be changed to a non-error level.

suggestions.label: behavioral-change
suggestions.suggestionContent: The ticker interval was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This is a behavioral change (cleanup runs 10x more frequently) and is not a declare-vs-use defect.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says 'SQLite has a parameter limit of 999,' but SQLite 3.32.0+ defaults to 32766, and the new test explicitly exercises batch size 32767. The code is being conservative by always inlining IDs when batch size exceeds 999 on SQLite, but the comment presents 999 as the current SQLite limit. Update the comment to explain that 999 is a safe conservative threshold or note the version-dependent limits, so the documentation matches the change's intent and the new test case.

suggestions.label: log-level smell
suggestions.suggestionContent: The logging uses r.log.Error for routine messages, which is a log-level smell. It does not throw, corrupt state, or violate an invariant, so it is not a defect in the assigned class, but the log level should likely be lowered (e.g., Info/Debug) for non-error routine messages.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags (e.g., 0x22) because it only masks the low 5 bits of the tag byte. WHY: DER/BER requires INTEGER to be primitive; accepting constructed encodings silently parses malformed input as a valid integer, diverging from BouncyCastle's strict parser. HOW: Reject the constructed bit by checking `(tag & ASN1Encoder.CONSTRUCTED) == 0` before reading the value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The ignored-providers log calls `logger.debugf(builder.toString())`, but debugf expects a format string. WHY: A provider class name containing `%` (e.g., from a shaded/proxied jar) would cause `MissingFormatArgumentException` and abort detection; even without that, it is the wrong logging API. HOW: Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` and avoid the trailing comma.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getBouncyCastleProvider returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, the JVM's default keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. WHY: This violates the CryptoProvider contract documented to return a BouncyCastle provider and misidentifies the provider in BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER/logs when AuthzClientCryptoProvider is selected. HOW: Return null so BouncyIntegration.loadProvider falls back to the first installed provider, which is the documented null-handling behavior.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates two ASN1Encoder instances at lines 114-115 and discards them. WHY: This is leftover dead code that allocates and encodes the integers before the real sequence encoding at lines 117-121; it performs no work and is misleading. HOW: Remove the two unused encoder calls.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test in ECDSAAlgorithmTest.test() only asserts that converting a signature DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS yields the same concatenated bytes twice. This round-trip assertion cannot detect a broken conversion that corrupts the signature symmetrically. The test should verify the re-encoded DER signature against the original data using Signature.verify() with the public key, or compare rsConcat to a value derived from the original sign, so the test fails if the ASN.1/RS conversion corrupts r or s.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The method name getBouncyCastleProvider() promises a BouncyCastle provider, but the implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the platform default keystore provider (usually SUN for JKS). This identifier/code disagreement can mislead callers that rely on BouncyCastle-specific behavior. Either return an actual BouncyCastle provider or rename the method/role to reflect that it provides a generic fallback provider.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The method assumes signature.length == signLength and copies signLength/2 bytes from it. A malformed or mismatched concatenated signature causes an unhandled ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Validate that signature is non-null, signLength is even, and signature.length == signLength before copying, throwing IOException for invalid input.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The method assumes signature.length == signLength. It allocates r/s of size len+1 and copies len bytes from signature without validation; a shorter input causes an out-of-bounds read. Add an explicit check (e.g., if (signature.length != signLength) throw new IOException(...)) before the array copies.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When qLength < bytes.length, the method copies only the lowest qLength bytes. For a malformed or non-minimal DER integer whose value exceeds the curve coordinate size, this silently changes the numeric value instead of rejecting the signature. It should throw if bytes.length > qLength + 1 (after allowing at most one sign-padding zero) or if stripping that zero still leaves more than qLength bytes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes Resource.getId() (the authorization resource UUID) to hasPermission and adds it to the returned set, but group-specific resources are looked up by name and their name is the group id. WHY: This causes user/group filtering to use authorization UUIDs instead of real group ids, breaking the UserModel.GROUPS filter, and group-specific view-members permissions are never evaluated because findByName fails on UUIDs. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() in both places, matching AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource which creates resources named after the group id.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The no-arg canManage() returns true if the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE scope on the global Groups resource. WHY: This violates the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract (manage should require MANAGE), so a view-only administrator is treated as having global group management rights and can pass requireManage() checks such as group creation. HOW: Evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE for the global canManage() check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), so any caller with only the 'view' scope on groups is treated as having global group management rights. This contradicts the GroupPermissionEvaluator interface contract, which limits canManage() to callers with the MANAGE_USERS role or permission to MANAGE groups. Because GroupResource/GroupsResource creation paths use requireManage() -> canManage(), a VIEW-only grantee could create groups. Remove AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW from the scopes checked in canManage() so it only requires AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The GroupPermissionEvaluator Javadoc for canManage() says access requires AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS or permission to MANAGE groups. The V2 implementation also accepts the VIEW scope, so a policy that only grants group view access would incorrectly allow group creation, update and deletion. Restrict the check to AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment on requireManageMembers references the wrong method (canManageMembership), which misleads callers about which capability is being enforced.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The @return tag says Stream, but the method signature returns Set<String>; update the prose so callers read the correct contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The interface Javadoc says VIEW/MANAGE permissions grant canView(), but the legacy GroupPermissions implementation only checks admin roles. Either implement the permission check in V1 or qualify the permission path as V2-only (as was done for canList) so the contract matches all implementations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking isPresent(), so a missing recovery-codes credential in both federated and local storage throws NoSuchElementException. WHY: This crashes the login form rendering when the credential is absent, instead of failing gracefully or redirecting to setup. HOW: Check credentialModelOpt.isPresent() before .get(), and throw a meaningful runtime exception or redirect if the credential is missing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After resolving a credential through RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, the code removes an exhausted credential via authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes locally stored credentials. WHY: When the credential lives in federated/user storage, removeStoredCredentialById cannot remove it, so the exhausted credential remains and the user is stuck with an unremovable credential or spurious re-configuration prompts. HOW: Distinguish federated vs local credentials; for federated credentials invoke disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE) or route removal through the user storage provider instead of removeStoredCredentialById.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated recovery codes to JSON and passes them as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel to user storage, while the local-storage path stores hashed codes through RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider. WHY: A user storage provider that persists the CredentialInput value (as the test BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does) stores recovery codes in plain text, exposing high-value backup credentials if the external store or its backups are compromised. HOW: Pass the codes in a form that lets the storage provider hash them before persistence, or document that user storage providers must hash the value themselves and update the test provider to hash before storing and compare hashed values during validation.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The recovery code verification uses direct String.equals() on hashed secrets, which is vulnerable to timing attacks. Use a constant-time comparison function (e.g., MessageDigest.isEqual) to compare the hashed input against each stored hashed recovery code.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The recovery key validation compares raw input recovery codes against stored values using key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()) inside a stream, which performs a non-constant-time comparison and leaks timing information. Use a constant-time comparison function for each candidate recovery code.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: createRecoveryCodesCredential passes the raw generatedCodes JSON to user storage via updateCredential, while falling back to the credentialModel (which holds hashed codes) for local storage. This creates a representation split: user-storage providers receive and typically store plaintext recovery codes, whereas the local DB provider stores hashed codes. The validation path in the test user storage then compares raw input to raw stored codes, inconsistent with the normal hashed validation. The method should pass equivalent credential material to both paths, e.g., by using the credential model's serialized/hashed data for user storage as well, or by documenting and enforcing that user-storage providers must hash the received codes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies the numeric Paginator implementation and calls math.floor/ceil on the raw key value. WHY: AuditLogEntry is ordered by '-datetime', so getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime object and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, crashing pagination for authorized users. HOW: Use DateTimePaginator-style conversion (strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier) before floor/ceil, or make OptimizedCursorPaginator inherit from DateTimePaginator.

suggestions.label: bug
